newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Broad-based dollar demand drove the rand two cents weaker on Thursday and pushed it close to the 4.70 level which dealers said was expected to be breached by Friday afternoon.
The currency settled at 4.6780/6830 against the dollar from 4.6600/6650 overnight and after touching a day's weakest level of 4.6840 bid during the morning session.
Dealers said both local and offshore players had been looking to buy dollars on the day.
"The market is looking really short...there is big demand out there. It's coming from everywhere," a dealer said.
One trader said a large local order for dollars had been the prime reason for the rand's continued weakness on the day.
What appeared to be Reserve Bank assistance above the 4.68 level kept the rand from weakening further on the day, but dealers said a 4.70 rand appeared likely in the immediate term.
Some traders predicted the level would be breached after the local close at 1400 GMT, while others said it was possible on Friday.
Against the crosses, the rand gained ground against sterling as cable's retracement continued.
It was last quoted at 7.5807/5935 against sterling from 7.6331/6459 on Wednesday and at 0.3323/3328 marks from 0.3349/3355.
On the bond market, yields shrugged off a worse-than-expected PPI figure to move largely sideways on the day.

Central Statistical Service data showed producer inflation rose 8.3 percent year-on-year compared with 7.6 percent in September. The latest figure was four points above a Reuters consensus forecast of a 7.9 percent rise.
"The PPI didn't do much and with the rand weak the bonds ended up looking pretty strong on the day," a trader said.
Other traders felt, however, that the data had been leaked and pointed to the fact that the market strengthened briefly shortly after the data was released at 0900 GMT.
"It was a bad number and the market had no reason to strengthen," one trader said.
Dealers said volumes on the day were generally thin. "We saw some foreign demand and the institutions looking to buy at the higher levels," one said.
They said that without any market-moving news in the short-term, the market was likely to hold in a 15.82 to 15.88 percent range.
The key R150 was last quoted at 15.85 percent from 15.81 percent on Wednesday.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates edged up to between 17.10 and 17.15 percent offered from 17.10 percent on Wednesday, while 90-day BAs were steady in a 16.40 to 16.65 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage up at 9.739 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.436 billion rand on Tuesday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net sellers of local bonds worth 32.79 million rand after buying bonds worth 378.05 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.62 billion rand from 5.87 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
